channel.title: Mullvad (and Tor) Browser default resolution makes you uniquely identifiable across VMs
channel.description:
I know that this is not in the kicksecure development scope, but i think that it is critical to investigate since mullvad is the premier browser outside of tor.
I found out that this website ai.updf. com can track me across virtual boxes instances while using mullvad browser. First i noticed it after using it on my home system. I made like 3-4 different chats closed the session and forgot about it, few weeks later i open another chat in the same site from mullvad and im back with my old conversations. In both instances i used vpn with different IPs.
So i decide to check what happens when i do it in virtual box. I create an ubuntu vm with fresh vpn and when i started a new chat it didnt sent me back to my old session. So far so good.
Well i decide to see what will happen on whon+Kick. I setup A whonix gateway + kicksecure VM, i install mullvad, I open a brand new chat and im in the same session as the one from my ubuntu VM. Everything was clean the whonix gateway the kick VM brand new unused, I even typed with diferent speed and the topics were completely different and thet that site managed to connect one ubuntu VM that was used with VPN, with another kicksecure VM that was used over tor.
The only conclusion i can deliver is that there seems to be a massive leaking of hardware identifiers by Mullvad browser.
And im singling it out because i do not get the leaks on brave, not on my home setup and not into my VMs. When i open new private brave every session opens brand new chat, I never get into a previous session with old chats.
EDIT.
**This is 10 times worse than i initially thought.** I Tested this with Whonix Work+ gateway stations on the Tor browser. I was uniquely identified and put into the same session on both Workstation VM's. I told a friend of mine to test this setup and he confirmed He also got tracked across multiple VM's.
To be precise It seems that X setup makes you uniquely identifiable on your machine across VM's. I got tracked on 3 instances of Mullvad across 3 vms(ubuntu+Kick+Kick) and separately on 2 instances of Tor across 2 workstation VMS It was not cross traceable from Mullvad to Tor. Brave seems to be unaffected.
EDIT 2
**Ok so after some testing I found out the reason** Its a "feature" not a bug Mullvad and tor give you browser window resolution that is supposed to make you blend with other users, well i guess that resolution will be the same for every VM on that specific browser for every single session unless you manually change the size of the window. When I change the browser window before i go to the website i dont get into my old session but a brand new clean one every time.
So let me make sense of this, if i leave the browser window in its default size im going to be traceable across the web, across VMs for that particular browser Tor or Mullvad. If i change it i become unique. What now?
